text:
Sales-Sam: quick one — Skyline Health pushing back on our 25% headroom for their dedicated commit in eu-west1. They want 10% to cut cost. Can infra run 4k GPU-hours/mo baseline (4xA100-ish) with a 10% buffer and still hit 99.9% p95 latency SLO for short chat workloads? They expect seasonal peaks up to ~6k GPU-hours. Need an answer by EOD.

Amira Patel: short answer: 10% is risky in eu-west1 right now. Two reasons: rack/gpu availability is constrained (we have 1 spare A100 rack in eu-west1 this quarter) and network oversubscription risk during bursts.

Zheng Li: putting some rough numbers — if we assume 1 A100 provides ~12 sustained qps for the customer's quantized chat model at target latency, 4 GPUs -> ~48 qps baseline. For peak -> need ~80 qps -> ~7 GPUs sustained. Simple calc:
```
baseline_hours = 4000
peak_hours = 6000
avg_gpus_needed_baseline = baseline_hours / (24*30) / 1   # rough
```
Not perfect, but you can see buffer below 15% requires burst credits or autoscale to avoid SLO hits.

Carla Mendez: also note networking — their workload has lots of KV cache misses early in sessions which multiplies p95 during spikes. In eu-west1 our NIC contention on the active racks shows +15-40ms tail latency under >70% node concurrency. If we compress buffer to 10% we should cap per-GPU concurrency + add a warmed KV pool.

Amira Patel: options we can offer the customer: 
- Option A (lower cost): 10% safety buffer + 20% monthly burst credits (pre-paid) + requirement to run 8-bit quantized variant; contract clause: if they exceed burst more than 3x in a month, we trigger a review and temporary rate limit.
- Option B (safer): 12% safety buffer + 10% burst credits, 3-month auto-review and infra-backed warm pool (we pre-warm 2 GPUs in eu-west1).
- Option C (multi-region): keep 10% buffer but allow failover to eu-west3 for up to 200 GPUs/mo of overflow (adds egress & cross-region cost).
Pick one and sales can negotiate.

Sales-Sam: sounds reasonable. customer will fight any extra cost. which option is lowest-cost for them but still safe for us?

Zheng Li: cheapest for them is Option A from infra OPEX perspective if they commit to quantized model and accept burst credits instead of reserved headroom. Rough delta vs a full 15% reserved buffer: ~-8% month1 cost for them, but operational risk increases. Compared to 10% no-burst (not recommended) we'd estimate infra OPEX +18% if we have to absorb unexpected spikes.

Carla Mendez: operationally I'd only accept Option A if we add two safety knobs: 1) per-node concurrency cap 12 reqs/gpu, 2) automatic KV-prefill for sessions that are flagged as high-rate. If they refuse, push for Option B.

Amira Patel: proposed contractual language snippet for Sales: "Redwood will provision dedicated capacity in eu-west1 with a baseline safety buffer of 12% and up to 20% burst credits for ad-hoc overage. Burst usage is subject to availability; Redwood reserves the right to route overflow to alternate region or to apply temporary throttles if capacity is exhausted." Sales: if they sign, infra will schedule pre-warm and set autoscale cooldown to 10m.

Sales-Sam: I'll propose Option B first (12% + 10% burst + 3mo review). If they push back I'll offer Option A as concession with the two safety knobs and an explicit rollback clause. Can you DM me a short one-paragraph cost delta I can paste in the quote?

Zheng Li: posted quick delta for quote: "Keeping 12% headroom vs 10% + bursts increases Redwood infra reserve costs by ~12-20% depending on GPU type and month; offering burst credits (10-20%) shifts ~8-12% of month-to-month variability onto customer billing. Precise numbers to be finalized after region sizing and model quantization confirmation."

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-4521 to track pre-warm work and region capacity check.

Amira Patel: ok — I'll run final eu-west1 capacity check (rack-by-rack) and confirm whether we can promise pre-warm for month-1. Expect an update in 2 hours.

Sales-Sam: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll flag this in the call with Skyline at 3pm. :thumbsup:
